raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Process CPU usage is not request latency. Add request-level wall-time histograms to show how much frontend processing occurs before a request is submitted to the Scheduler.

## Modifications

- Add one histogram, `sglang:frontend_request_stage_seconds`, controlled by the existing `--enable-metrics` flag, with `total`, `text`, and `multimodal` stages.
- Measure total time from HTTP route handler entry, before body parsing, until the frontend send returns. Record each logical request only on its first submission; exclude internal parallel-sampling warmups and pre-submission failures.
- Record text/MM only for requests that executed the stage, including genuine zero-duration observations. Their counts and percentiles describe participating requests, while total counts all submitted requests. No extra labels or counters.
- Carry request-local context through Chat conversion, multimodal executors, and dynamic batch tokenization. Shared batch execution is attributed in full to each participating request; encoding queue waits are excluded.
- Merge overlapping intervals within each stage. Text may overlap multimodal processing; fused template-and-encode operations remain in text. Stage durations and marginal quantiles must not be added. Send completion does not prove Scheduler receipt.
- Use `msgspec.Struct` for the new timing state, with independent span maps and locks per request. Timing attributes on internal requests/futures remain optional at existing lifecycle boundaries; metrics-disabled requests do not create timing objects.

## Accuracy Tests

Fresh UV development-host verification of commit `6ec732d52b8e61bb5bf80778b6b28f6157331c22`: exported and SHA256-verified an independent source snapshot, confirmed imports came from that snapshot, and ran the registered fail-fast entry points with uv 0.11.4 / Python 3.12.13. All 24 tests passed (6 timing + 9 metrics + 9 Chat); total process wall time including imports was 42.64 seconds. The archive SHA256 and the five directly checked source/test hashes matched. This is CPU validation (PyTorch 2.14.1+cpu), without a server, model load, or GPU replay.

```bash
uv run --no-project --active python test/registered/unit/observability/test_frontend_request_timing.py -f
uv run --no-project --active python test/registered/unit/observability/test_frontend_request_metrics.py -f
uv run --no-project --active python test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_chat_prompt_round_trip.py -f
```

24 CPU tests and 2 subtests passed in 23.88 seconds on the final source. The 12 relevant source/test files matched the execution environment by SHA256. Coverage includes request/thread isolation, batch attribution, first-submission deduplication, disabled metrics, Chat cache/render boundaries, skipped stages, genuine zero durations, failed/cancelled dispatch, and Prometheus multiprocess collection.

The skipped-stage regression was also run with the pre-fix observer restored: it fails because ten requests were counted instead of the two participating requests; the corrected implementation passes.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/observability/test_frontend_request_timing.py \
  test/registered/unit/observability/test_frontend_request_metrics.py \
  test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_chat_prompt_round_trip.py
```

The changed Python files pass the pinned isort 7.0.0 and ruff 0.15.1 checks, including formatting and F401/F821/F823/UP037. The full upstream [Lint workflow](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41627297086) passed on this head, including all-file pre-commit, PR title, and documentation link checks. No model-output algorithm is changed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No inference-speed improvement or universal inequality with TTFT is claimed. A six-request GPU correctness smoke test passed on the same final head `6ec732d52b8e61bb5bf80778b6b28f6157331c22` using an isolated UV development-host environment and local Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 weights (CUDA runtime SM90, Torch 2.14.1+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.2, sglang-kernel 0.4.10). Twelve relevant source/test hashes matched the execution snapshot. This was not a throughput or performance benchmark.

After built-in warmup completed, ran two text Chat requests, one text `/generate`, one pre-tokenized `/generate`, and two image Chat requests, with generation capped at 8 tokens. All six returned tokens; both images were correctly identified as red/blue (64 image tokens each). Raw `/metrics` snapshots before/after each request verified cumulative bucket increments, duration sums and `+Inf == count`.

Sample deltas were total=6, text=4, multimodal=2, TTFT=6, E2E=6. Pure text added no MM samples, token IDs added no text samples, and the second image reused the normalized Chat template encoding cache and added no explicit text-encoding sample. Optional stages were not zero-filled. Frontend totals were 0.50–7.01 ms and were below their matching TTFT on every request. Image cases measured total/MM/TTFT of 7.01/4.41/208.36 ms and 6.07/4.04/208.68 ms. The first formal request had a cold TTFT of 3.44 seconds. MM measures frontend processing, excluding Scheduler-side vision encoder GPU work.

An exploratory attempt overlapping startup warmup was excluded; the formal run waited for the final ready log before its baseline. The task-owned localhost server was stopped and the GPU returned idle (no compute processes; 4 MiB). No production service or existing environment was modified.

An earlier backport completed an isolated 600-second mixed replay with all 32 responses successful (18 text-only, 14 image requests; generation capped at 16 tokens). That run preceded the optional-stage population correction: its equal stage counts and zero-filled MM quantiles do not validate the final participating-request population. The final population and container changes are covered by the CPU tests and GPU smoke test above.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with the repository's pinned isort/ruff checks; full all-file pre-commit and GitHub lint passed.
- [x] Add focused CPU tests using `CustomTestCase`, standard entry points, and CI registration under `test/registered/unit/`.
- [x] Document timing boundaries, overlap, sample populations, and histogram aggregation.
- [x] GPU correctness smoke test of the final revision; no throughput benchmark or inference speedup claimed.
- [x] Follow the applicable `.claude/rules` and contribution guide, including `msgspec.Struct` for new containers.

Full test CI requires the upstream `run-ci` label; local CPU results above are independent of that gate. No deployment is part of this PR.

@@ -0,0 +1,32 @@
+# Request-level frontend wall time
+
+`sglang:frontend_request_stage_seconds{stage="total|text|multimodal"}` records
+each logical request once on its first submission to the Scheduler. Enable with
+`--enable-metrics`. `total` records every submitted request; `text` and
+`multimodal` record only requests that executed the stage. An executed stage with
+zero measured duration is still recorded.
+
+- `total`: HTTP route handler entry, before body parsing, until the frontend send
+  returns. Excludes routing before the handler and does not prove Scheduler receipt.
+- `text`: union of explicit encoding-call intervals for this request. Excludes
+  queue waits and separate template rendering; inseparable template-and-encode
+  calls include rendering. Shared batch execution is attributed in full to each
+  participant. Cache hits and pre-tokenized inputs do not add encoding intervals.
+- `multimodal`: the complete awaited local processor operation, including internal
+  waiting and nested text encoding. Base/Qwen explicit encoding is also recorded
+  in `text`; opaque fused processor calls are not artificially split.
+
+Stages may overlap and cannot be added to infer total elapsed time. Histogram
+quantiles describe different requests and must not be added either. Internal
+parallel-sampling cache warmups do not add request samples.
+
+Stage counts are participating request counts. Stage averages and quantiles
+describe those requests, not all submitted requests. Failed or cancelled stages
+retain their elapsed spans, but a request that never reaches submission does not
+export any of these samples.
+
+Use this histogram's sum/count for averages. For P50/P90/P99, aggregate buckets
+by model and stage before `histogram_quantile(0.5|0.9|0.99, ...)`. An absent
+metric or a window without requests should not be displayed as a synthetic zero.
+Existing TTFT can start at a later boundary and is observed on first-token
+arrival, so being below TTFT is not a proof of correct instrumentation.

+"""Request-local wall-clock spans for frontend timing.
+
+Intervals are merged within each stage so concurrent calls do not count the
+same wall-clock instant twice. Different stages may overlap and must not be
+added to infer the overall elapsed time.
+"""
+
+import contextvars
+import time
+from _thread import LockType
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+from threading import Lock
+
+import msgspec
+
+current_frontend_timing = contextvars.ContextVar(
+    "frontend_request_timing", default=None
+)
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def bind_frontend_timing(timing):
+    token = current_frontend_timing.set(timing)
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        current_frontend_timing.reset(token)
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def measure_frontend_stage(timing, stage):
+    if timing is None:
+        yield
+        return
+    start = time.perf_counter()
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        timing.add_span(stage, start, time.perf_counter())
+
+
+class FrontendRequestTiming(msgspec.Struct):
+    started_at: float
+    _spans: dict[str, list[tuple[float, float]]] = msgspec.field(default_factory=dict)
+    _lock: LockType = msgspec.field(default_factory=Lock)
+    _finished_at: float | None = None
+
+    def finish(self, finished_at):
+        """Claim the logical request's first submission exactly once."""
+        with self._lock:
+            if self._finished_at is not None:
+                return None
+            if finished_at < self.started_at:
+                raise ValueError("request end precedes request start")
+            self._finished_at = finished_at
+        return self.snapshot(finished_at)
+
+    def fork(self):
+        """Copy work shared before a batch was split into logical requests."""
+        with self._lock:
+            return FrontendRequestTiming(
+                started_at=self.started_at,
+                _spans={stage: list(items) for stage, items in self._spans.items()},
+            )
+
+    def add_span(self, stage: str, started_at: float, finished_at: float) -> None:
+        if finished_at < started_at:
+            raise ValueError("span end precedes span start")
+        with self._lock:
+            self._spans.setdefault(stage, []).append((started_at, finished_at))
+
+    def snapshot(self, finished_at: float) -> dict[str, float]:
+        """Return elapsed time and the union of each stage's clipped spans."""
+        if finished_at < self.started_at:
+            raise ValueError("request end precedes request start")
+        with self._lock:
+            spans = {stage: list(items) for stage, items in self._spans.items()}
+        durations = {"total": finished_at - self.started_at}
+        for stage, items in spans.items():
+            clipped = sorted(
+                (max(start, self.started_at), min(end, finished_at))
+                for start, end in items
+                if end > self.started_at and start < finished_at
+            )
+            total = 0.0
+            previous_end = self.started_at
+            for start, end in clipped:
+                total += max(0.0, end - max(start, previous_end))
+                previous_end = max(previous_end, end)
+            durations[stage] = total
+        return durations
+
+
+class FrontendTimingGroup:
+    """Attribute shared batch execution to every participating request."""
+
+    def __init__(self, timings):
+        self.timings = [timing for timing in timings if timing is not None]
+
+    def add_span(self, stage, start, end):
+        for timing in self.timings:
+            timing.add_span(stage, start, end)

+    def test_executed_zero_duration_stages_are_observed(self):

+    def test_failed_or_cancelled_dispatch_does_not_export_stage_spans(self):

+                self.assertAlmostEqual(timing.snapshot(11.0)["multimodal"], 0.1)

+                    cancel_for_dispatch=Mock(),

+                manager._dispatch_to_scheduler = Mock(side_effect=error_type())
+                request = SimpleNamespace(
+                    rid="request",

+                    "sglang.srt.managers.tokenizer_manager.wrap_shm_features",
+                    side_effect=lambda obj: obj,

+                self.assertIsNone(timing._finished_at)
+                for stage in ("total", "text", "multimodal"):
+                    self.assertIsNone(
+                        self.registry.get_sample_value(
+                            _METRIC + "_count",

+
+    def test_chat_encoding_excludes_separate_render_decode_and_cache_hits(self):

+    def test_fused_template_remains_text_without_extra_stage(self):
+        server = SimpleNamespace(

+        )

+    def test_async_batch_attributes_execution_to_each_request_without_queue_wait(self):
+        entered, release = threading.Event(), threading.Event()
+        batcher = AsyncDynamicbatchTokenizer(self.tokenizer)
+        timings = [
+            FrontendRequestTiming(started_at=0.0),
+            FrontendRequestTiming(started_at=0.0),
+        ]
+
+        def block_executor():
+            entered.set()
+            if not release.wait(10):
+                raise TimeoutError("test did not release executor")
+
+        async def run():
+            loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
+            blocker = loop.run_in_executor(batcher._executor, block_executor)
+            self.assertTrue(await asyncio.to_thread(entered.wait, 5))
+            futures = [loop.create_future(), loop.create_future()]
+            for future, timing in zip(futures, timings):
+                future._frontend_timing = timing
+            pending = asyncio.create_task(
+                batcher._process_dynamic_batch(["first", "second"], [{}, {}], futures)
+            )
+            await asyncio.sleep(0)
+            self.clock.value += 1.0

+            await blocker
+            await pending
+            return [future.result() for future in futures]

+        try:
+            with patch(_CLOCK, self.clock):
+                result = asyncio.run(run())
+        finally:
+            release.set()
+            batcher._executor.shutdown(wait=True)
+        self.assertEqual(result, [{"input_ids": [5]}, {"input_ids": [6]}])
+        for timing in timings:
+            self.assertAlmostEqual(timing.snapshot(self.clock.value)["text"], 0.04)

+"""Check request-local timing with nested and overlapping operations."""
+
+import asyncio
+import unittest
+from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
+from contextvars import copy_context
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+from sglang.srt.multimodal.processors.executor import MultimodalProcessorExecutor
+from sglang.srt.observability.frontend_request_timing import (
+    FrontendRequestTiming,
+    FrontendTimingGroup,
+    bind_frontend_timing,
+    current_frontend_timing,
+    measure_frontend_stage,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class TestFrontendRequestTiming(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_multimodal_executor_keeps_request_context_isolated(self):
+        first = FrontendRequestTiming(started_at=10.0)
+        second = FrontendRequestTiming(started_at=10.0)
+        executor = MultimodalProcessorExecutor(lambda: {}, max_workers=1)
+
+        def encode(duration, *, processor):
+            timing = current_frontend_timing.get()
+            if timing is not None:
+                timing.add_span("text", 10.0, 10.0 + duration)
+            return timing
+
+        async def submit(timing, duration):
+            with bind_frontend_timing(timing):
+                return await executor.run(encode, duration)
+
+        async def run():
+            results = await asyncio.gather(submit(first, 0.1), submit(second, 0.2))
+            self.assertEqual(results, [first, second])
+            self.assertIsNone(await executor.run(encode, 0.5))
+
+        try:
+            asyncio.run(run())
+        finally:
+            executor.shutdown()
+        self.assertAlmostEqual(first.snapshot(11.0)["text"], 0.1)
+        self.assertAlmostEqual(second.snapshot(11.0)["text"], 0.2)
+
+    def test_batch_forks_keep_shared_work_and_isolate_later_spans(self):
+        parent = FrontendRequestTiming(started_at=10.0)
+        parent.add_span("text", 10.0, 10.1)
+        first, second = parent.fork(), parent.fork()
+        FrontendTimingGroup([first, second]).add_span("text", 10.2, 10.4)
+        first.add_span("multimodal", 10.5, 10.7)
+        self.assertAlmostEqual(first.snapshot(11.0)["text"], 0.3)
+        self.assertAlmostEqual(second.snapshot(11.0)["text"], 0.3)
+        self.assertNotIn("multimodal", second.snapshot(11.0))
+        self.assertAlmostEqual(parent.snapshot(11.0)["text"], 0.1)
+
+    def test_encode_span_follows_request_into_executor(self):
+        request = FrontendRequestTiming(started_at=10.0)
+
+        def encode():
+            with measure_frontend_stage(current_frontend_timing.get(), "text"):
+                pass
+
+        with patch(
+            "sglang.srt.observability.frontend_request_timing.time.perf_counter",
+            side_effect=[10.2, 10.4],
+        ):
+            with (
+                bind_frontend_timing(request),
+                ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) as pool,
+            ):
+                pool.submit(copy_context().run, encode).result()
+        self.assertIsNone(current_frontend_timing.get())
+        self.assertAlmostEqual(request.snapshot(11.0)["text"], 0.2)
+
+    def test_request_span_union_preserves_cross_stage_overlap(self):
+        request = FrontendRequestTiming(started_at=10.0)
+        request.add_span("text", 10.2, 10.5)
+        request.add_span("text", 10.4, 10.6)
+        request.add_span("multimodal", 10.3, 10.8)
+        durations = request.snapshot(11.0)
+        self.assertAlmostEqual(durations["total"], 1.0)
+        self.assertAlmostEqual(durations["text"], 0.4)
+        self.assertAlmostEqual(durations["multimodal"], 0.5)
+
+    def test_spans_are_clipped_to_request_lifetime(self):
+        request = FrontendRequestTiming(started_at=1.0)
+        request.add_span("text", 0.0, 1.5)
+        request.add_span("text", 2.5, 4.0)
+        self.assertEqual(request.snapshot(3.0)["text"], 1.0)
+
+    def test_rejects_invalid_intervals(self):
+        request = FrontendRequestTiming(started_at=1.0)
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            request.add_span("text", 2.0, 1.0)
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            request.snapshot(0.5)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
